s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic inflammatory syndrome with fever, fatigue, and abdominal tenderness, progressing over several days
salient_findings: Tenderness in the left lower quadrant
Nonspecific inflammatory changes on CT imaging
Dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate on peritoneal biopsy
key_facts: Four days of fevers, fatigue, nausea, headaches, and malaise
Blood pressure of 82/50 mm Hg (responded to fluids)
Nonspecific inflammatory fat stranding and peritoneal thickening on CT
Peritoneal biopsy showed dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD8, CD7, CD43, CD5 (partial loss), TIA-1, granzyme B, CD2, and TCRβ F1

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ferritin, fever, and histiocytic infiltration on biopsy

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Peritoneal biopsy showed dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate and immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD8, CD7, CD43, CD5, TIA-1, granzyme B, CD2, and TCRβ F1

shortlist.label: T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD8, CD7, CD43, CD5, TIA-1, granzyme B, CD2, and TCRβ F1, and elevated interleukin (IL)-2R alpha levels

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammatory syndrome with fever, fatigue, and abdominal tenderness, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Adult-onset Still's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, fatigue, and abdominal tenderness, and elevated ferritin and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with prolonged fevers, elevated ferritin levels, and evidence of hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy, along with elevated interleukin (IL)-2R alpha levels, are key indicators of Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). The patient's laboratory results, including significantly elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT), low leukocyte count, and thrombocytopenia, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While the peritoneal biopsy showed a dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate, which could suggest a lymphoma, the overall clinical and laboratory picture, including the systemic nature of the illness and the specific findings like very high ferritin levels and hemophagocytosis, points more towards HLH than a primary diagnosis of subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Similar to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, the presence of a T-cell lymphoid infiltrate could suggest T-cell lymphoma, but the systemic symptoms and specific laboratory findings such as elevated ferritin and evidence of hemophagocytosis are more indicative of HLH.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While SLE can present with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities, the specific combination of findings in this patient, particularly the very high ferritin levels, evidence of hemophagocytosis, and the absence of other classic SLE criteria, makes HLH a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adult-onset Still's disease
rejected.why: Adult-onset Still's disease can present with fever, rash, and systemic inflammation, but the presence of significantly elevated ferritin levels, hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy, and the specific immunohistochemical findings are more characteristic of HLH than adult-onset Still's disease.

gold: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (SPTCL) with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)
